title: New roads shifted work out of farming in one Indian study
body: In a 2020 study of India's rural road programme, Sam Asher and Paul Novosad found that new feeder roads moved some workers out of agriculture. Four years after construction, they found no major change in village incomes or assets.
takeaway: A road can change what people do for work before producing a measurable change in how much they earn.
source: Asher and Novosad, American Economic Review (2020)

title: A US tax credit expansion drew more single mothers into work
body: A study of the 1986 US tax reform compared single women with and without children. After the reform expanded the Earned Income Tax Credit, participation in paid work rose among single mothers relative to the comparison group.
takeaway: A policy can affect the decision to start working differently from the number of hours people already work.
source: Eissa and Liebman, Quarterly Journal of Economics (1996)
visual: a plain payslip turned face down beside a time clock
